name: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman
bio: Led the Awami League through the Six-Point autonomy campaign, the 1970 electoral mandate, and the March 1971 crisis that shaped Bangladesh's independence struggle.
impact: Turned language rights, autonomy, and electoral representation into a mass demand for Bengali self-determination and statehood.

name: Syed Nazrul Islam
bio: Served as acting president of the Provisional Government of Bangladesh in 1971 while Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was imprisoned in Pakistan.
impact: Gave the wartime state constitutional continuity and helped frame the Liberation War as a legitimate national struggle.

name: Tajuddin Ahmad
bio: Led Bangladesh's first government as prime minister during the Liberation War, organizing Mujibnagar governance, diplomacy, and wartime strategy.
impact: Turned dispersed resistance into a state-led independence struggle with political legitimacy, military coordination, and external support.

name: Muhammad Mansur Ali
bio: Served in the Mujibnagar government, later became prime minister of Bangladesh in 1975, and is remembered as one of the Four National Leaders killed in jail.
impact: Connects wartime national leadership with postwar state-building and the memory of the 1975 Jail Killing.

name: A. H. M. Qamaruzzaman
bio: Served as home affairs leader in the Provisional Government of Bangladesh and helped administer wartime political authority in 1971.
impact: Strengthened the wartime government structure and is remembered as one of the Four National Leaders killed in jail in 1975.

name: M. A. G. Osmani
bio: Commanded the Bangladesh Forces during the Liberation War and shaped the sector-based military structure of the Mukti Bahini.
impact: Gave organized command, strategy, and national military identity to the liberation forces.

name: Ziaur Rahman
bio: Broadcast the declaration of independence from Kalurghat on behalf of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and later commanded Sector 1, Sector 11, and Z Force.
impact: Combined early symbolic visibility with organized military command during the Liberation War.

name: Khaled Mosharraf
bio: Commanded Sector 2 and later K Force during the Liberation War, organizing regular-force and guerrilla operations around a strategic theatre.
impact: Helped define the operational strength of one of the war's most important sectors.

bio: Khudiram Bose is listed among notable historical figures in this project timeline.

bio: Charu Majumdar is listed among notable historical figures in this project timeline.

name: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
bio: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad is listed among notable historical figures in this project timeline.
impact: Influenced anti-colonial constitutional thought, education policy, and pluralist political discourse.

name: Syed Ahmad Khan
bio: Syed Ahmad Khan is listed among notable historical figures in this project timeline.
impact: Influenced Muslim educational reform and constitutional political thought in colonial South Asia.

name: Ivy Rahman
role: Awami League leader and August 21 attack victim
bio: Ivy Rahman was a senior Awami League organizer who died from injuries sustained in the 21 August 2004 grenade attack.
impact: Her death remains central to public memory of political violence in early-2000s Bangladesh.

name: Mufti Abdul Hannan
role: HuJI-B militant leader and convicted attacker
bio: Mufti Abdul Hannan was identified in security reporting as a HuJI-B leader and was executed after conviction in the Sylhet attack case.
impact: His cases became central to public understanding of militant prosecutions and counter-terrorism politics.

name: Siddique ul-Islam (Bangla Bhai)
bio: Siddique ul-Islam, widely known as Bangla Bhai, became a prominent militant organizer in northwestern Bangladesh.
impact: His activities made militant violence in the northwest a national security issue in the mid-2000s.

name: Henry Louis Vivian Derozio
role: Teacher, poet, and early Bengal Renaissance intellectual
bio: At Hindu College he encouraged critical inquiry among students later associated with the Young Bengal circle.
impact: His short teaching career became a marker of new secular, rationalist, and reformist currents in colonial Bengal.

name: David Hare
role: Education reformer in early colonial Calcutta
bio: Supported modern education institutions that formed the setting for later reform and Young Bengal debates.
impact: His work helped institutionalize English and modern education in Bengal's urban public sphere.

name: Debendranath Tagore
bio: Helped consolidate Brahmo reform currents after Rammohun Roy and shaped Bengal's nineteenth-century religious-intellectual life.
impact: His leadership gave institutional continuity to reformist religious and philosophical debate in Bengal.

name: Keshab Chandra Sen
role: Brahmo Samaj reformer and public speaker
bio: Expanded Brahmo reform debates into wider social, religious, and public reform questions.
impact: He made Brahmo reform a more visible part of public controversy and social reform discourse.

name: Pulin Behari Das
bio: Associated with revolutionary organizing in eastern Bengal, especially Dhaka Anushilan circles.
impact: His organizing illustrates the eastern Bengal branch of militant anti-colonial politics.

name: United Front
role: Opposition Electoral Alliance in East Bengal
bio: The United Front won the 1954 East Bengal election on a broad autonomy and 21-point programme.
impact: Its victory broke Muslim League dominance in East Bengal and strengthened the path from language politics toward autonomy.

name: National Awami Party
bio: National Awami Party linked Bhashani's mass politics with anti-Ayub protest, left-nationalist organizing, and Farakka mobilization.
impact: It kept peasant, left, and anti-imperial themes visible in East Pakistan and Bangladesh mass politics.

name: Bangladesh Krishak Sramik Awami League
bio: BAKSAL was the one-party political restructuring introduced in Bangladesh in 1975.
impact: Its formation and collapse became central to debates over state power, party rule, and democratic breakdown.

name: Communist Party of India
bio: The Communist Party of India shaped Bengal left politics through labour, peasant, and Tebhaga-era organizing.
impact: Its networks made class, land, and peasant rights central to twentieth-century Bengal politics.

name: Hindu Mahasabha
bio: Hindu Mahasabha was a major Hindu political organization in late-colonial Bengal partition debates.
impact: Its Bengal position helped make partition of the province a central alternative to a united Bengal.

name: Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal
role: Former home minister linked to security-force accountability debates
bio: Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal was Bangladesh's home minister during major protest-control and security-crackdown periods.
impact: His tenure is tied to public debates over security-force deployment, command responsibility, and 2024 crackdown accountability.

name: Benazir Ahmed
role: Former RAB director general and police chief
bio: Benazir Ahmed is a former RAB director general and Bangladesh police chief named in the 2021 U.S. Treasury sanctions action.
impact: His designation made RAB-linked rights-abuse allegations an international accountability issue.

name: Ziaul Ahsan
bio: Ziaul Ahsan is a security and intelligence-linked figure repeatedly named in public allegations around disappearance, detention, and surveillance.
impact: His profile connects security-sector command structures to post-2024 debates over secret detention, digital monitoring, and accountability.

name: Rao Farman Ali
bio: Rao Farman Ali is linked in Bangladesh memory and reporting to Operation Searchlight planning and allegations around the intellectual killings.
impact: His name remains central to debates over command responsibility and the planning of mass violence in 1971.

name: Khadim Hussain Raja
bio: Khadim Hussain Raja is reported as one of the officers who worked on the plan that became Operation Searchlight.
impact: His profile identifies the command-planning layer behind the March 1971 crackdown.

name: Jahanzeb Arbab
bio: Jahanzeb Arbab is included as a brigade-level Pakistan Army commander associated with 1971 operations in East Pakistan.
impact: His profile connects Operation Searchlight planning with field command and implementation.

name: Mir Quasem Ali
role: Jamaat and Al-Badr-linked war-crimes case figure
bio: Mir Quasem Ali was convicted in a 1971 war-crimes case tied to Al-Badr activity in Chittagong.
impact: His case became a major node in debates over 1971 justice, tribunal process, and Jamaat politics.

name: Chowdhury Mueen Uddin
bio: Chowdhury Mueen Uddin was convicted in absentia by ICT-2 in the December 1971 intellectual-killings case.
impact: His case became one of the central tribunal records connecting Al-Badr to the targeted killing of intellectuals.

name: Ashrafuzzaman Khan
bio: Ashrafuzzaman Khan was convicted in absentia by ICT-2 in the December 1971 intellectual-killings case.
impact: His case is central to tribunal memory around targeted intellectual killings and Al-Badr involvement.

name: ATM Azharul Islam
role: Jamaat leader in contested war-crimes proceedings
bio: ATM Azharul Islam was convicted by the ICT in a 1971 case, but later reporting says the Appellate Division acquitted him.
impact: His case illustrates how 1971 justice and appellate review remained contested long after the tribunal verdict.

name: Abul Kalam Azad (Bachchu Razakar)
bio: Abul Kalam Azad, known as Bachchu Razakar, was sentenced in absentia in the first Bangladesh ICT verdict over 1971 crimes.
impact: His distinct profile avoids confusion with Maulana Abul Kalam Azad and marks the opening judgment in the ICT process.
